login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Welcome back. Sign in to manage your devices.
login.totpSubtitle: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
login.useLocal: Sign in with a local account

password.mismatch: The new passwords do not match.
password.rules: At least 12 characters, not containing your username. A sentence of a few words works well.

totp.step1: Open an authenticator app such as Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or 1Password.
totp.step2: Scan the QR code, or enter the key by hand, and type the code it shows.
totp.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app

firstLogin.title: Choose a new password
firstLogin.subtitle: You signed in as {{user}} with a one-time password. Choose your own password to continue.
firstLogin.totpSubtitle: Your password is changed. We recommend two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, especially for the administrator account.

profile.title: Profile
profile.subtitle: Your account, language and security.
profile.twoFactorHint: A code from an authenticator app is asked after your password.
profile.totpDisableHint: Enter your password to turn off two-factor authentication.
profile.managedByEntra: You sign in with Microsoft Entra ID; multi-factor authentication is handled there.
profile.passwordSaved: Your password is changed. Other sessions were signed out.

users.title: Users & roles
users.subtitle: Local accounts and accounts that signed in with Entra ID. Roles decide what each person may do.
users.name: Name
users.roleFromEntra: Set by the role mappings at every Microsoft sign-in.
users.breakGlassRole: The emergency account is always an administrator.
users.initialPasswordHint: Leave empty to generate a one-time password. The user must choose a new password at the first sign-in.
users.disableHint: A disabled user cannot sign in; open sessions end right away.
users.resetHint: {{user}} gets a new one-time password and is signed out everywhere.
users.oneTimeHint: Give this password to {{user}} in a safe way. It is shown only once and must be changed at the first sign-in.
users.rolesSubtitle: Built-in roles and what they allow. Technicians and read-only users can be limited to device groups.
users.scopeFromEntra: The device groups come from the role mappings at every Microsoft sign-in.

roles.administratorDesc: Everything, including users, settings and updates.
roles.technicianDesc: Manage devices: patches, software, remote control.
roles.readonlyDesc: View the dashboard, devices and reports.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.subtitle: Local accounts always work. Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on is optional and off by default.
auth.entraSubtitle: Let people sign in with their Microsoft work account.
auth.enableHint: The local emergency administrator keeps working.
auth.tenantIdHint: Entra admin center > Overview > Tenant ID
auth.clientIdHint: From the overview page of your app registration.
auth.clientSecretHint: The secret value (not the secret ID) from Certificates & secrets.
auth.redirectUriHint: Add this as a Web redirect URI in the app registration. Set the public URL under Settings if it is wrong.
auth.testOk: Connection works: the tenant was found and the client secret is accepted.
auth.breakGlassSubtitle: The local "admin" account always stays available as a break-glass account. You can limit where it may sign in from.
auth.networksHint: Comma-separated IP addresses or CIDR ranges. Empty means everywhere. Your address now: {{ip}}
auth.mappingsSubtitle: Map Entra groups or app roles to FleetWarden roles. Roles are checked again at every sign-in.
auth.noMappings: No mappings yet. Without a mapping nobody can sign in with Microsoft.
auth.mappingsNote: When someone matches several mappings, the most privileged role wins. Users in more than 200 groups: use app roles.

mail.title: Mail server
mail.subtitle: Your own SMTP server for notifications, reports and alerts.
mail.enableHint: Queued messages are sent once mail is on.
mail.noneWarning: Without encryption, messages travel in clear text. Only use this for a relay on the local network. Password authentication is then not allowed.
mail.oauthHint: Uses the client credentials flow. The app registration needs the Exchange Online permission SMTP.SendAsApp and access to the mailbox in the username field.
mail.heloHint: Optional; the server host name by default.
mail.logSubtitle: The last 200 messages. Failed messages are retried up to 6 times.
mail.subject: Subject

branding.title: Branding
branding.subtitle: Your own name, logo and colours for the interface, the sign-in page and e-mails.
branding.productNameHint: Shown in the menu, the browser tab and e-mails. Empty: FleetWarden.
branding.logoHint: Square works best. SVG or PNG, up to 512 KB.
branding.faviconHint: Optional. Without one, the logo is used.

updates.title: Updates
updates.subtitle: Choose the update channel and update the server from here. A backup is made before every update, and a failed update is rolled back.
updates.channelHint: Production follows main; Test follows the test branch with the newest features.
updates.none: No release on this channel yet
updates.switchToProductionHint: You run a test build. Production updates are offered once production has a newer version than yours.
updates.confirm: Update to {{version}}? The server makes a backup, installs the update and restarts. The interface is unavailable for about a minute.

states.pending: Waiting for the updater to start…
states.rolled-back: Update failed and was rolled back

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: General server settings and updates.
settings.publicUrlHint: The address people use through your reverse proxy, used for SSO and links in e-mails. Empty: detected as {{url}}.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.subtitle: Who did what and when: sign-ins, changes to users and settings, and updates.
audit.search: Search user, action, target or IP

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.subtitle: Encrypted full and incremental backups of the database and server files to one or more locations, with restore from the interface.
backup.runHere: Back up to this location now

setup.passBody: Every backup is encrypted with your passphrase before it leaves the server. Without it, backups cannot be made or restored.
setup.locBody: Choose where backups go: an SFTP/SCP or FTPS server, OneDrive, or a folder on this server such as a mounted network share.

stat.retention: Keeps {{count}} full backups with their incrementals

backup.locationsHint: Every backup goes to all enabled locations. Use at least one location outside this server.
backup.deleteLocationBody: Delete the location {{name}}? Backups already stored there are not removed and can still be restored with "Another location".
backup.noLocationsHint: Add an SFTP/SCP, FTPS or FTP server, a OneDrive, or a local folder.

typeHints.sftp: Any server with SSH access: a NAS (Synology, QNAP), a Linux server or a hosting account. Works wherever scp works.
typeHints.ftps: FTP with TLS encryption, for example FileZilla Server or a NAS. Self-signed certificates can be trusted after a test.
typeHints.ftp: Plain FTP. The backup itself is encrypted, but the password travels unencrypted.
typeHints.onedrive: Stores backups in the OneDrive of a Microsoft 365 user through an Entra app registration.
typeHints.local: A folder under /var/lib/fleetwarden/backups on this server, for example a mounted NAS share. Not a replacement for an off-site copy.

loc.name: Name
loc.implicitTlsHint: Only for servers that expect TLS right away (usually port 990). Most servers use explicit TLS on port 21.
loc.keyHint: Generate a key pair and add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the backup user on the server, or paste your own private key.
loc.publicKeyHint: Add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the backup server.
loc.onedriveHint: Uses an app registration in Microsoft Entra with the application permission Files.ReadWrite.All (admin consent). You can use the same app as for sign-in. See docs/backup.md for the steps.
loc.driveUserHint: User principal name of the account whose OneDrive stores the backups.
loc.pathHint: Folder on the server, relative to the home or root folder. Created when it does not exist.
loc.enabledHint: Disabled locations are skipped but can still be used for a restore.
loc.ftpWarning: FTP sends the password unencrypted. Use FTPS or SFTP when the server supports it.

trust.sshBody: The server presents this SSH host key. Compare it with the fingerprint on the server before you trust it.
trust.tlsBody: The server presents a certificate that is not issued by a trusted authority (for example self-signed). Check the SHA-256 fingerprint before you trust it.

repo.none: No backups at this location yet; the first backup creates the repository.
repo.wrong_passphrase: This location already holds FleetWarden backups made with another passphrase. Use another folder.
repo.unknown: Writing and deleting a test file works.

pass.title: Encryption passphrase
pass.subtitle: Backups are encrypted (AES-256) on this server with a key derived from this passphrase.
pass.warn: Store it in your password manager. To restore on a new server you need the passphrase; without it nobody, including you, can read the backups.
pass.label: Passphrase
pass.hint: At least 12 characters. A sentence works well.
pass.changeHint: Existing backups at reachable locations are re-keyed, so they can be restored with the new passphrase.

sched.title: Schedule and retention
sched.subtitle: Automatic backups: incremental ones in between, regularly a new full backup.
sched.enableHint: Missed backups (server off) run once when the server is back.
sched.fullEveryHint: The backups in between are incremental.
sched.keepHint: Older ones are deleted with their incrementals.
sched.summary: A full backup every {{full}} days, {{keep}} kept: you can go back about {{days}} days.

restore.title: Restore
restore.subtitle: Put the database and server files back from a backup. Also works on a new server: install FleetWarden, sign in and pick "Another location".
restore.otherHint: Enter the location and passphrase of the original server.
restore.passHint: The passphrase the backups were made with.
restore.snapshotsHint: Newest first. A full backup and its incrementals form a chain; each one can be restored on its own.
restore.newer: This backup was made with FleetWarden {{version}}, newer than this server. Update this server first.
restore.confirmBody: All current data (users, settings, history) is replaced by the backup. Everyone is signed out and the server restarts. A copy of the current state is kept on the server for a rollback.
restore.applyingBody: The server is restoring the backup and restarts. You will be taken to the sign-in page.
restore.stuck: Nothing happening? On a server without systemd, run the restore by hand:
restore.prepareFailed: The backup could not be prepared

backup.historyHint: The last 200 backups. A restore starts a new history.

scope.limitedHint: Only devices in the selected groups are visible and manageable.
scope.noneSelected: No group selected: this user sees no devices.

devices.title: Devices
devices.subtitle: Every enrolled workstation, server and Proxmox node, with live status and inventory.
devices.searchPlaceholder: Search name, user, IP, serial or OS
devices.emptyHint: Use Add client to get an installer and a ready-made command for Windows or Debian/Proxmox.
devices.selectAll: Select all devices on this page
devices.inventoryRequested: The agent is collecting a new inventory.
devices.deleteConfirm: Delete {{host}} and its inventory? A connected agent stops and forgets its enrollment; to manage the machine again, enroll it again.
devices.findOthers: Show every device with this program
devices.notesHint: Free text for your team, for example location or owner.
devices.noPackages: There are no packages for this platform in the library yet. Add one under

addClient.title: Add client

platformHints.windows: Windows 10/11 and Windows Server 2016 or newer
platformHints.linux: Debian 12/13, Ubuntu and Proxmox VE (amd64, arm64)

addClient.groupHint: New devices join this group. Each group gets its own token.
addClient.tokenUnusable: This token is revoked, expired or used up. Create a new one.
addClient.windowsCommand: Windows: run in an elevated PowerShell
addClient.windowsCommandHint: Downloads the MSI from this server, installs it silently and enrolls the device.
addClient.msiexec: Unattended install with msiexec (GPO, Intune, RMM)
addClient.linuxCommandHint: Downloads the .deb from this server, installs it and enrolls the device.
addClient.noPackage: This server has no agent package for this platform yet. Agent packages arrive with the server package or from Agent updates.
addClient.downloadHint: The server address and token are built into the download, so a double-click is enough.
addClient.manualHint: The installer wizard asks for these values:
addClient.waiting: Waiting for the device to enroll…

tokens.descriptionHint: Helps you recognise the token later, for example "Intune rollout".
tokens.title: Enrollment tokens
tokens.subtitle: Tokens let agents enroll into a group. Revoke a token when a script or installer leaked; enrolled devices keep working.
tokens.empty: No tokens yet. Add client creates one.
tokens.revokeConfirm: New devices can no longer enroll with this token. Devices that already enrolled are not affected.

groups.title: Groups
groups.subtitle: Device groups decide policies, update rings and which devices a role may manage.
groups.name: Name
groups.notEmpty: Move the devices out of this group first.
groups.ringHint: New agent versions reach ring 0 first, then the next rings.
groups.channelHint: For example a test group of pcs on the Test channel.
groups.windowLimit: Only update agents in a time window
groups.windowHint: Server time. A window like 22:00–06:00 runs past midnight.
groups.patchPolicyHint: When and how updates are installed on the devices in this group.

agentUpdates.title: Agent updates
agentUpdates.subtitle: New agent versions come from GitHub or an upload and reach the device groups ring by ring.
agentUpdates.checked: Checked GitHub for new agent releases.
agentUpdates.rolloutsHint: A rollout starts with ring 0 (pilot). The next ring follows after the soak time; too many failed devices pause it.
agentUpdates.noOpenRollout: No rollout is running. Every agent runs the version its group should have.
agentUpdates.soakSummary: {{hours}} h per ring, pause after {{failures}} failures
agentUpdates.problemsHint: The agent reinstalled its previous version where it could. Use Retry on the rollout after fixing the cause.
agentUpdates.releasesHint: Groups without their own agent channel follow the server channel ({{channel}}). Production groups only receive releases.
agentUpdates.noReleases: No agent packages yet. Check GitHub or upload a package.
agentUpdates.startHint: Devices with an older agent receive this version, ring 0 first. A running rollout on the same channel is replaced.
agentUpdates.deleteConfirm: Delete the packages of version {{version}} from the server? Agents on this version can then no longer roll back to it.
agentUpdates.autoDownloadHint: Checks every hour for the channels your groups use.
agentUpdates.autoRollout: Start a rollout for each new release
agentUpdates.autoRolloutHint: Off: new versions are only downloaded, and you start rollouts yourself.
agentUpdates.soakHint: How long each ring runs before the next ring.
agentUpdates.maxFailuresHint: Failed devices per ring before the rollout pauses.
agentUpdates.keepReleasesHint: Older downloads are removed unless devices still run them.

patches.title: Patch management
patches.subtitle: Missing updates, approvals and maintenance windows for Windows, Debian and Proxmox.
patches.noPolicyText: Devices are only patched when their group has a patch policy.
patches.scanErrors_one: {{count}} device could not scan for updates. Open the device for the error.
patches.scanErrors_other: {{count}} devices could not scan for updates. Open the device for the error.

categoryHints.security: Security fixes, also security packages on Debian and Proxmox.
categoryHints.cumulative: Monthly cumulative updates and update rollups.
categoryHints.other: Other updates, and regular apt updates on Linux.

patches.missingUpdatesHint: Across all devices you may see. Approve or decline an update for every device at once.
patches.policiesHint: Assign a policy to device groups under Groups.

rebootHints.never: The device reports that it needs a restart; you restart it yourself.
rebootHints.automatic: Restarts right after installing. A logged-on user sees a countdown first.
rebootHints.prompt: The user may postpone the restart; after the last postpone it restarts anyway.

patches.deletePolicyConfirm_one: Delete {{name}}? {{count}} group will no longer be patched.
patches.deletePolicyConfirm_other: Delete {{name}}? {{count}} groups will no longer be patched.
patches.enabledHint: When off, devices still scan on request but nothing is installed automatically.
patches.windowHint: Jobs only start inside the window; a window may run past midnight. Devices that are offline get their updates in the next window.
patches.approvalsHint: Automatic approval can wait a number of days after release, so problems with an update show up first. A manual approval or decline under Updates always wins.
patches.notifyUsersHint: Before installing, Windows shows a pop-up at the bottom right. Restarts always show one. Without a logged-on user the job goes ahead right away.
patches.countdownHint: Without an answer the job goes ahead.
patches.takeOverHint: Turns off Windows' own automatic installs, so updates only arrive in the window. Devices that get updates from Intune or a WSUS GPO: choose one tool to be in charge.
patches.deviceNoPolicy: This device's group has no patch policy. Set one under
patches.scanRequested: The device is scanning for updates.
patches.installStarted: The patch job was sent to the device.
patches.upToDate: Up to date: no missing updates.

software.title: Software
software.subtitle: Your software library, and everything installed across your devices.
software.libraryHint: Packages you can roll out to devices and groups.
software.emptyText: Add software from the winget catalog, upload your own MSI or EXE installer, or add an apt package for Linux.
software.deleteText: Delete {{name}} from the library? Software that is already installed stays on the devices, and past deployments keep their history.

catalog.title: Winget catalog
catalog.hint: The server downloads the public winget catalog once a day. Devices download installers straight from the vendor and check the SHA-256 hash from the catalog.

software.installedHint: From the inventory of every device you can see. Uninstall removes the program from every device that has it, or the devices you pick.

kinds.exeHint: Enter the silent install arguments from the vendor.
kinds.debHint: Installed with apt-get, which also fetches the dependencies.

deploy.platformHint: Only devices with this platform are shown.
deploy.ongoing: Keep the groups up to date
deploy.ongoingHint: Devices that join these groups later get the job too.
deploy.uninstallArgsHint: Optional. FleetWarden uses the quiet uninstaller when the program has one, and msiexec /x for MSI packages. Add the vendor's silent arguments here when it doesn't.
deploy.purgeHint: Uses apt-get purge instead of remove.
deploy.laterHint: Pick when the devices may start.
deploy.expireHint: Devices that haven't started by then are marked as expired.

source.wingetHint: Search thousands of applications. Always the official installer from the vendor.
source.uploadHint: Your own MSI or EXE for Windows, or a .deb for Linux.
source.aptHint: A package from the repositories your Linux devices already use.

form.aptPackageHint: The exact package name, such as htop or curl.
form.noInstaller: This package has no installer FleetWarden can run silently for all users.
form.versionHint: Latest always installs the newest version from the catalog.
form.catalogEmpty: The winget catalog hasn't been loaded yet. Close this window and refresh the catalog first.
form.searchCatalog: Search the winget catalog, such as Chrome or 7-Zip
form.dropFile: Drop an installer here (.msi, .exe or .deb, up to {{size}} GB)
form.argsWinget: Optional. Added to the silent arguments from the catalog.
form.argsMsi: Optional MSI properties, such as ALLUSERS=1 or a license key.
form.argsRequired: Required. Find the silent arguments in the vendor's documentation, such as /S or /quiet.
form.name: Name
form.fileVersionHint: Optional. Devices with this version or newer are skipped.
form.detectNameHint: Used to see if the program is already installed. Defaults to the package name.
form.productCodeHint: Optional. The most precise way to detect an MSI.
form.anyHashHint: Some vendors replace the installer behind the same link (such as Chrome). Turn this on only for vendors you trust.

deployments.title: Deployments
deployments.subtitle: Software installs and uninstalls, with the result of every device.
deployments.emptyText: Pick a package in the software library and choose Deploy.
deployments.cancelled: The deployment is cancelled. Jobs that are running finish first.
deployments.rebootNeeded_one: {{count}} device needs a restart to finish.
deployments.rebootNeeded_other: {{count}} devices need a restart to finish.
deployments.cancelText: Devices that haven't started won't run this job. Jobs that are already running finish first.
deployments.rebootText: The installer asked for a restart. The device restarts in the next maintenance window, or you can restart it yourself.
